meta.title: Wild Ohio
meta.summary: A marsh at sunrise, a forest path, a river bend… Ohio has plenty of reasons to slow down. Let’s trade the checklist for a little patient looking—and enjoy the quiet. ♡

sourceRefs.label: Ohio Department of Natural Resources · Parks guide

blocks.text: Ahh, Lake Erie wetlands, prairie remnants, hardwood forests, rivers, and sandstone gorges give Ohio a surprising range of habitats. State parks, Wayne National Forest, and Cuyahoga Valley National Park offer different ways into that landscape. Hiking, paddling, camping, or simply sitting somewhere green all count. You’re allowed a quiet adventure; there’s no hurry when the small details are part of the visit.

What you see depends on place and season. Migrating birds use the lakeshore; forests shelter deer, wild turkeys, and smaller creatures; streams and wetlands support their own busy worlds. Follow park guidance, stay on marked paths, and give wildlife space. A good sighting feels even better when the animal gets to carry on undisturbed. I’m happiest with enough time to notice one patch properly. A quiet walk doesn’t need to be an empty one. ♡
